text: On an ECP5 CIC missing 150 MHz at 131.1 MHz with the critical path in the un-staged N=3 comb-subtractor carry chain (comb_d 4.89 ns of 7.63 ns) and pipelined integrator, adding reg_in gave only 133.0 MHz (+1.9 MHz, unchanged 0 LUT/0 DSP) and stayed infeasible because the path remains that comb chain plus output truncation, so pipeline the comb subtractor rather than just the input.

When an ECP5 CIC is timing-limited at 133 MHz by the unstaged N=3 comb subtractor carry chain (22 cells, 4.89 ns) plus output truncation on a 7.52 ns path, insert pipeline registers between the comb stages to reduce it to one 25-bit subtractor per cycle, raising Fmax to 271.8 MHz (+138.8 MHz) for only +5 LUTs and no DSPs.

On an ECP5 CIC whose critical path is the combinational subtractor carry chain (22 cells, 3.68 ns from c_x[1] through c_x[2]), don't register only the input sample to close timing: it shifts the wall to the next carry stage (24 cells, 3.72 ns, c_x[2] to c_x[3]) and costs 3 MHz (271.8 -> 268.8 MHz) plus 1 LUT with no feasibility gain—pipeline the comb chain itself instead.

For a feasible ECP5 CIC (N=3, B=25, 268.8 MHz, LUT near floor) whose critical path is a single 25-bit carry chain, do not remove the integrator/comb pipeline registers to test full unrolling: it serializes the integrator and comb carry chains (13+14 cells, 13.23 ns), collapsing Fmax to 75.6 MHz and losing feasibility for only 6 LUT saved.

On the ECP5 CIC, when timing is limited by a 13.23 ns carry-chain path through integ[0] and comb_d[0], enable pipe_comb to insert an inter-stage register and split that chain, raising Fmax from 75.6 to 125.2 MHz (+49.6 MHz) for +5 LUT and 0 DSP—still below 150 MHz, so it helps but does not close timing.

When an ECP5 CIC is already feasible with the critical path in the 25-bit integrator carry chain rather than the input pads, do not add an input register (reg_in=false→true) to try to gain timing: it cuts only one carry cell (16→15) and c_x carry cells (11→9), adds 1 LUT, and lowers Fmax by 1.7 MHz (125.2→123.5), because the cascaded carry chain still dominates and the extra route delay offsets the removed cell.
